ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there are two input terminals A and B, both entering a logic block labeled “&”; the output terminal of this logic block has a small circle, indicating output inversion. Then the signal enters a logic block on the right that has only one input and is labeled “1”; this block outputs to F, and its output terminal also has a small circle, indicating inversion again. Reasoning: The first block labeled “&” is an AND gate, so the signal before the small circle at its output is A·B. The small circle at the output terminal of the AND gate turns it into ¬(A·B). The later single-input block is not combined with any other signal, and the small circle at its output terminal inverts once again, so F = ¬[¬(A·B)] = A·B.

method.method_draft: Identify the first block as an AND gate, so before its output bubble the signal is A·B. The bubble at the AND output changes this to ¬(A·B). The following one-input block does not combine it with any other signal, and its output bubble inverts it again. Therefore F = ¬[¬(A·B)] = A·B.
